about.text: Milk sugar is the filler that gives tablets and capsules their bulk and lets the powder flow and press. Different grades are made by drying a lactose suspension in a spray, gluing fine crystals into granules, or dehydrating the crystals.

facts.v: Fine milled alpha-lactose monohydrate suspension spray-dried; 10-15 % amorphous lactose, which deforms plastically and binds the tablet; introduced 1950s-60s
Coarse flow plus fine-milled compactibility in one grain (Tablettose 70, 80, 100)
Mostly beta crystal, non-hygroscopic, for moisture-sensitive drugs and dry granulation (DuraLac H)
